articles.title: The Dangers of Getting Advice from the Internet
articles.summary: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice online and recognize the danger of letting AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ.
articles.summary_zh: Melissa和Courtney讨论了如何在网上寻求建议时培养洞察力，并认识到让人工智能或影响者取代基督身体的明智建议的危险。
articles.title_zh: 从互联网上获取建议的危险
articles.content: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice. They talk about how sometimes we think we need information when what we really need is relationship. They discuss what kind of advice they like to get from the internet or ChatGPT, why they don’t recommend it for wisdom issues such as marriage and parenting, and why we shouldn’t let advice from AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ. Resource Mentioned: Kitchen-Table Counseling Within Your Local Church Related Resources: Let’s Talk: Finding a Mentor and Being a Mentor Want to Grow in Wisdom? You Need Gospel Friends. Why AI Parenting Advice Falls Short Don’t Treat AI as Your Pastor Discussion Questions: 1. When you face a difficult decision or struggle, where do you typically turn for advice? 2. How do you discern whether online advice is helpful or unwise? 3. What makes advice offered within a personal relationship different from advice taken from an online blog or influencer or generated by AI? 4. How might repeated exposure to ideas about marriage, parenting, or relationships on social media influence our thinking without us being aware of it? 5. What do we lose when we turn to online sources for counsel instead of investing in relationships with people who know and love us? 6. Who in your life knows you well enough to speak honestly into your decisions and loves you enough to do so? How can you cultivate those kinds of relationships? 7. How would you like to grow in your ability to offer wise counsel to others?
articles.content_zh: Melissa和Courtney讨论如何在寻求建议时培养辨识力. 他们谈论我们有时认为我们需要信息, 当我们真正需要的是关系。 他们讨论他们喜欢从网络或ChatGPT获得什么样的建议, 为何不推荐给婚姻及养育等智慧问题, 资源参考:在您当地教会的相关资源中提供厨房-餐桌咨询:让我们谈谈:寻找导师和成为导师想要在智慧中成长? 你需要福音的朋友。 为何AI的家长建议会落下, 2. 你如何辨别在线建议是否有益或不明智? 3. 个人关系中提供的建议与在线博客或影响者或大赦国际提供的建议有何不同? 4. 在社交媒体上反复接触关于婚姻、养育子女或关系的想法会如何影响我们的思想,而我们却不知道这一点? 5. 当我们转向在线律师来源而不是投资于与了解和热爱我们的人的关系时,我们会失去什么? 6. 在你的生活中,谁足够了解你 诚实地谈论你的决定, 并爱你 足够这样做? 你怎么能养成那种关系? 7. 如何提高你向他人提供明智建议的能力?

articles.title: Beware Making Mental Illness an Identity
articles.summary: ‘All in Your Head’ is a concrete and compelling remapping of mental health culture with impressive explanatory power.
articles.summary_zh: “All in Your Head”是对心理健康文化的具体而引人注目的重新映射，具有令人印象深刻的解释力。
articles.title_zh: 小心让精神疾病成为一种身份
articles.content: In the years since he was involuntarily committed to a mental health institution for bipolar disorder, Frederik deBoer has wrestled with both profound gratitude for a system that saved his life and also palpable frustration that his experience of healing has become so rare. All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to Be Disordered is the latest broadside from one of the internet’s most heterodox thinkers and writers. As an “old school” Marxist best known for writing The Cult of Smart , deBoer takes aim at how the cultural drift within his own tribe is responsible for making mental health care so elusive for those who need it most: “The tendency to treat mental illness as an exciting adventure, the endless romanticization of lunacy in popular culture, is one of many aggravations I have nursed for years” (8). The root of his aggravation—the treatment of mental illness and disability as an identity to be celebrated rather than a disability that needs treatment —isn’t all in his head. The use of talk therapy rose 47 percent between 2019 and 2024 . A 2025 LifeStance survey found around 29 percent of U.S. adults have self-diagnosed their mental health condition after consuming online content, rising to 50 percent among Gen Z (versus 9 percent of boomers). Of the people who self-diagnose symptoms, almost a quarter (24 percent) “rarely” or “never” feel the need to take the next step to discuss them with a qualified clinician. DeBoer argues that rather than reducing the stigma surrounding mental illness, the inordinate attention given to the mildly and dubiously afflicted is a dangerous distraction crowding out help for the severely ill. Accelerated by social media, this “gentrification of disability” has become a full-blown social contagion, compromising even the experts and institutions responsible for mental health care (153–54). DeBoer is largely right, and the cultural shift he identifies has real-world implications both inside and outside the church. But the same ideological priors that so sharpen deBoer’s critique also suffer from two significant blind spots that, were they addressed, would make All in Your Head the more courageous, more constructive, and, therefore, more widely read manifesto we need. General Bipartisan Ire If you picked up All in Your Head to understand how modern therapy culture spread like wildfire across social media over the last several years, it’s not immediately obvious why deBoer starts his argument with an in-depth analysis of the anti-psychiatry movement’s influence in late 20th century politics and academia. But, if you can forgive me the pun, there’s a method to his madness. After a blistering critique of “rightwing libertarian” policies that neglected mental illness, he cashes in on the subsequent trust he earns with left-leaning readers to launch a series of absolute haymakers toward “a species of thought that sometimes amounts to a kind of leftist pseudo-radicalism or a libertarian fantasy” (198) that drives the “destabilizing . . . move from mental illness as reality to mental illness as symbol” (8). American individualism and anti-institutional bias aren’t new, but the painstakingly specific way deBoer traces their spread through the culture surrounding mental health and therapy is refreshing and instructive. Our “apolitical romanticism of resistance to modern society” fuels two opposite errors: On the right, mental illness is sometimes seen as either imagined or a symptom of weak character. But on the left, the same romanticism often describes mental disability as more en abling than dis abling, as if neurodivergent minorities don’t need society’s help—society needs theirs. Gentrification of Disability DeBoer’s emphatic rejection of this predominantly progressive error— of “making a medical disorder an identity”—is the “overarching principle of [his] book” (165). articles.content_zh: 在他非自愿地被送入精神病院治疗两极分化后的几年里,弗雷德里克·德·博尔带着对挽救他生命的系统深表感谢和明显的沮丧,因为他的治愈经验变得如此罕见. 在你的脑海中:作为身份的疾病,作为时尚的创伤,以及希望陷入混乱,是互联网上最异形的思想家和作家之一的最新一面。 作为一位最以写作"聪明的邪教"而出名的"老派"马克思主义者,德博尔以自己的部落内部的文化漂移为目的,让那些最需要的人如此难以接受精神保健:"将精神疾病视为激动人心的冒险的倾向,在流行文化中无休止地浪漫化的放荡,是多年来我所照顾的诸多恶化之一"(8). 他的病情恶化的根源——将精神疾病和残疾视为一种值得庆贺的身份,而不是需要治疗的残疾——并不是他脑子里所有的东西。 2019年至2024年间,谈话疗法的使用率上升了47%. 2025年生活稳定调查发现,约29%的美国成年人在消费了在线内容后自行诊断出自己的心理健康状况,在Gen Z中上升到了50%(相对于9%的繁荣者). 在自我诊断的人群中,近四分之一(24%)的人“勉强”或“从未”感到有必要采取下一步措施,与合格的临床医生讨论这些症状。 DeBoer认为,对受轻度和可疑折磨的人的过度关注,与其减少精神疾病的污名化,不如说是一种危险的分心,挤出对重病患者的帮助。 社交媒体加速了这种 " 残疾意识化 " ,已成为一种全面的社会传染,甚至损害负责精神保健的专家和机构(153-54)。 DeBoer基本上是正确的,他所认定的文化转变在教堂内外都具有现实世界的影响. 但德布尔批评如此尖锐的意识形态前科也遭遇了两个重大盲点,如果这些盲点得到解决,将使你的头脑更加勇敢,更具建设性,因此,我们需要更广泛地阅读宣言。 一般两党爱尔兰人 如果你在脑海中看到现代治疗文化在过去几年里如何像野火一样在社交媒体上传播,那么DeBoer为什么以深入分析20世纪后期反精神病运动在政治和学术界的影响为出发点,这并不明显。 但是,如果你能原谅我的双关语,他疯狂是有办法的。 在对忽视了精神疾病的“右翼自由派”政策猛烈批评后,他依靠后来与左翼读者获得的信任,发动了一系列绝对的干草人,走向“有时相当于一种左翼伪激进主义或自由派幻想的思想”(198年),这种思想驱使“从精神疾病变成现实,转变为精神疾病作为象征”(8)。 美国的个人主义和反机构偏见并非新事物, 但DeBoer通过精神卫生与治疗的文化, 我们“反对现代社会的政治浪漫主义”助长了两个相反的错误: 在右边,精神疾病有时被视为一种想象或一种弱性症状. 但是在左边,同样的浪漫主义常常将精神残疾描述为比分身更困难,仿佛神经分身的少数民族不需要社会的帮助——社会需要他们的帮助。 对DeBoer残疾人的强烈反对,即 " 使医疗障碍成为身份 " 这一主要进步的错误,是 " 书中的首要原则 " (165)。 这在他所称的“残疾的基因化”中再清楚不过了。

articles.title: How a Former Prisoner in Iran Wants You to Pray for Christians in Chains
articles.summary: Pray not only for what God might do for Christian prisoners in Iran but for what God might do through them, for his glory.
articles.summary_zh: 不仅祈求神可以为伊朗的基督徒囚犯做些什么，而且祈求神可以通过他们为祂的荣耀做些什么。
articles.title_zh: 伊朗前囚犯如何希望你为被锁的基督徒祈祷
articles.content: Not long ago, I had a surreal phone call with two young Christian men serving prison sentences in one of Iran’s hardest prisons. They’re there because they refuse to stop preaching about Jesus. When I asked how I could pray for them, their answer wasn’t what you might expect. “Pray that we would not be released until our job here is finished,” they said. They had led numerous fellow prisoners to faith. Now, their chief concern was to remain inside long enough to disciple them. The call took me straight back to the five years I spent in prison for my faith. Now, these dear brothers (let’s call them Vahid and Reza) were behind bars, and I was outside. As we spoke, I pictured the wards and corridors, imagined the sounds and smells, and remembered how hard it was not to know how many years I would be there. But it was also an encouraging call. Vahid and Reza were in high spirits, talking about Bible passages that were sustaining them and how the Lord was at work. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. Their focus was the same as Paul’s in Colossians 4:3: “Pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in prison.” Paul’s request wasn’t for an open prison door but for an open door for the gospel. Pray for Gospel Fruit Vahid and Reza’s request resonated with me. I remember being unable to pray for my own release. I tried on a few occasions, but I couldn’t open my mouth to ask the Lord to release me. If I’m following Christ, I cannot choose the path. I cannot choose the location. I should follow him wherever he goes. And as I followed him to prison, he brought beautiful fruit. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. I think of one prisoner, a devout Muslim, who was wrongly accused of spying for Iran’s enemies. He was praying he would be released and was frustrated to get no answer. He approached me one day, saying, “Farshid, our God is dead. But I’ve heard yours is alive. Will you pray for me?” Fearing it might be a trap, I took him quietly aside and prayed briefly in the name of Jesus: “Lord, you know this man. Please hear his prayer.” The very next day, the man rushed over excitedly and gave me a huge hug. That morning, he had learned his name had been cleared. He was released two weeks later. Our God is indeed alive. The Lord was also at work softening my parents’ hearts toward Christ during those years. I always say that even if only for the salvation of my parents, my time in prison was worth it. So, when you pray for persecuted believers, pray not only for what God might do for them but—as Vahid and Reza requested—for what God might do through them, for his glory. Pray for gospel fruit. Pray for Comfort and Endurance I don’t want to make prison sound easier than it was. The suffering was real. So pray also for comfort and endurance. They beat me; they broke my toe. But the prolonged separation from my two children was the hardest burden to bear. The day I went to prison, my son was 2 years old and my daughter was 7. Missing their childhoods was an unspeakable loss. Yet I know others who have suffered much more than I did. I think of a brother currently in prison who has been tortured. I think of a sister who was sexually assaulted when she was arrested. Even the apostle Paul was at times “so utterly burdened beyond [his] strength that [he] despaired of life itself.” And his request to the church was simple: “You also must help us by prayer” (2 Cor. 1:8, 11). Brothers and sisters like these need us to pray for them with love. Whatever the situation, we can pray that God would grant the suffering believer comfort, peace, and endurance. The more specific the prayers, the better. While in prison, I received letters from people around the world who were praying for me. One wrote, “I am praying for your sleep. May the Lord give you
articles.content_zh: 不久前,我和两名基督教青年在伊朗最困难的监狱之一服刑。 因为他们拒绝停止宣扬耶稣。 我问自己如何为他们祈祷, 他们说,“祈祷我们在这里的工作结束前不会被释放。” 他们带领许多同狱囚犯信仰。 现在,他们最关心的是 留在里面的时间足够长 让他们入门。 那通电话把我带回我为信仰在监狱里度过的五年。 现在,这些亲爱的兄弟(让我们叫他们Vahid和Reza)在监狱里,我在外面。 就在我们发言的时候,我想象了病房和走廊,想象了声音和气味,并想起了不知道我会在那里呆了多少年是多么困难。 但这也是一个令人鼓舞的呼吁。 瓦希德和礼萨精神高尚,谈论着支撑着他们的圣经段落,以及上帝是如何工作的. 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。 他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 他们的重心与保罗在Colosisans 4:3中的重心相同 : “ 也为我们祈祷,以便上帝为我们打开一个话语之门,宣告基督之谜,我为此而入狱。 ” 保罗的要求并不是打开监狱的门, 祈求福音果实Vahid, 我还记得我无法为自己的自由祈祷 我尝试过几次, 我无法选择道路。 我无法选择位置 我该跟着他 不管他去哪 当我跟着他进监狱时 他带来了美丽的水果 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。 他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 我想到一个囚犯, 一个虔诚的穆斯林, 他祈祷自己会被释放,并因得不到答复而感到沮丧。 有一天,他靠近我说,“法尔希德,我们的神死了。 但我听说你还活着。 你会为我祈祷吗?” 我担心那可能是一个陷阱,悄悄地把他放在一旁,以耶稣的名义简短地祈祷道:"主啊,你认识这个人。 请听他的祈祷。” 第二天,那个男人激动地冲过来,给了我一个巨大的拥抱。 那天早晨,他得知自己的名字已被清除。 他两周后被释放。 我们的神确实还活着。 在那些年中,上帝也在努力使我父母对基督的心软化。 我总是说,即使只是为了拯救我的父母, 我在监狱的时间是值得的。 当你们祈祷受迫害的信士们的时候,你们应当祈祷真主所意欲者,犹如瓦希德和里萨所意欲者那样,祈祷真主所意欲者。 祈取福音果实. 祈祷舒适与耐力, 苦难是真实的。 因此也祈求安慰和耐力. 他们打我,把我的脚趾弄断了 但是,与我的两个孩子长期分离是最难承受的负担。 我入狱那天,我的儿子2岁,女儿7岁。 失去童年是一个难以形容的损失。 然而,我认识其他人,他们遭受的痛苦比我多得多。 我想到目前在监狱里的一个兄弟 曾遭受酷刑 我想到一个妹妹在被捕时曾被性侵犯. 甚至使徒保罗,有时也“承受了超过他力量的沉重负担,以致于他对生命本身绝望”。 他向教堂提出的要求很简单:“你还必须通过祈祷帮助我们”(第1:8、11节)。 这样的兄弟姐妹需要我们用爱为他们祈祷. 无论情况如何,我们可以祈祷上帝会给予受苦受难的信徒以安慰、和平和耐力。 祈祷越具体越好 在狱中,我收到了世界各地为我祈祷的人的来信。 有人写道:“我在为你的睡眠祈祷。 愿主赐予你

articles.title: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches
articles.summary: While thousands of Americans are dechurching, some churches are baptizing many new members. Here’s how the country’s most evangelistically effective churches are sharing the gospel.
articles.summary_zh: 虽然成千上万的美国人正在脱离教会，但一些教会正在为许多新成员施洗。以下是这个国家最有效传福音的教会分享福音的方式。
articles.title_zh: 传福音有效教会的最佳实践
articles.content: https://media.thegospelcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/23102213/effective-evangelism.mp3 In the summer of 2021, pastor Luke Peterson moved to Columbus, Ohio, to look for lost people. To find them, he joined a gym. He started building friendships. And then he began asking those friends if they wanted to come over. “Word started getting around—‘You’re not going to believe this, but Luke’s a pastor,’” he said. ‘It created some intrigue, and people started coming. I used to have a note in my phone of how many people came to our church because I went to CrossFit Grandview. It was up to like 60 or 70 before I stopped counting because it was impossible.” Peterson’s good at evangelism, and his church is too—last year, they welcomed around 500 first-time visitors. When he preaches, he knows about half his audience is probably unchurched. Pastor Luke Peterson (right) chats with Capital Church attendees / Courtesy of Capital Church Facebook This is unusual in a country where 40 million adults have stopped attending church over the last 30 years, and where 76 percent of pastors said “fostering connections with unchurched people” is a need in their church. Much has changed since the Billy Graham rallies of the ’60s, the door-knocking of the ’80s, and seeker-sensitive church billboards of the ’90s. In the past, “you could randomly walk up to the person pumping gas next to you and say, ‘Do you know Jesus?’” said Perimeter Church pastor Jeff Norris. “Could that still work? Sure. But more and more, we tell people to invite neighbors into their home. The reality is that evangelism is much slower, and more relational, than it used to be.” Today, people aren’t as likely to read the Bible, think it’s the Word of God, or go to church . But they’re also less hostile to Christianity than they were five years ago. And while they read the Bible less—especially in Gen Z—the trajectory is moving up . “We’re not past ‘my truth, your truth,’” said Rob Warren, pastor of Doxa Church in Madison, Wisconsin. “But people aren’t as sure that their truth is actually true.” These days, evangelistically effective churches are keeping evangelism front of mind in the way they preach, train, and encourage their congregations. They’re celebrating small wins. And they’re leading with a high view of Scripture, prayer, and God’s sovereignty. “We’ve seen all of our ministries grow—from kids to youth to college ministry to Doxa Church as a whole,” Warren said. “It’s not just one demographic of people who are getting saved. God’s doing something.” Times Have Changed Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said . Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said . “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. “I’ve got a new couple that moved into my neighborhood a while ago, and I haven’t even seen them yet,” said Daniel Simmons, executive pastor of campuses and central discipleship at The Summit Church. This means equipping the congregation is more challenging—and important—than ever before. “Evangelism can be this thing that is so burdensome and guilt-driven,” said pastor Christian Gracia. articles.title: We Need to Know Our Reformed Roots
articles.summary: This volume is an invitation to rediscover that heritage and to find fresh encouragement in the faithfulness of God, who has sustained his church through the centuries.
articles.summary_zh: 这本书邀请我们重新发现这一遗产，并在神的信实中找到新的鼓励，神几个世纪以来一直支持他的教会。
articles.title_zh: 我们需要了解我们的改革根源
articles.content: What does it mean to be Reformed? The label is used frequently but not always carefully. For some, it simply refers to a particular view of salvation. For others, it evokes a tradition, a culture, or even an aesthetic. Yet historically, to be Reformed has meant something much richer. While no single sentence can capture the fullness of the Reformed tradition, at minimum it means three things: to be biblical, to be covenantal, and to be confessional. The authority of Scripture governs our theology, covenant theology provides Scripture’s redemptive framework, and the historic confessions summarize and safeguard the church’s doctrinal convictions. Remove any one of those pillars, and something essential to the Reformed tradition is lost. With “Reformed” in its name, it’s hardly surprising that Reformed Theological Seminary has long sought to equip pastors and church members in all three areas. In recent years, members of its faculty have produced substantial volumes on the Old and New Testaments and on covenant theology. Now, with The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application , they turn their attention to the confessional foundation of the Reformed tradition. The result is a volume that seeks not only to explain what the confession teaches but also to demonstrate why confessional theology remains vital for the church today. What Is the Westminster Confession of Faith? The Westminster Confession of Faith takes its name from the Westminster Assembly, a gathering of more than 100 ministers and theologians convened by the English Parliament in 1643 at a time of profound political and ecclesiastical upheaval. The assembly was tasked with recommending reforms to the doctrine, worship, government, and discipline of the Church of England. After more than five years of careful biblical study and theological deliberation, the assembly produced the Westminster Confession of Faith along with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms. Together, these documents have served as the doctrinal foundation of Presbyterian churches throughout the world for nearly four centuries. The assembly’s influence, however, extends far beyond Presbyterianism. The confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. As a result, its theological influence shaped generations of Congregationalists, Baptists, and other evangelical Christians. The editors of this volume rightly observe, The confession is also ecumenical because it found wide acceptance among Congregationalists and Particular Baptists in the seventeenth century, as two different groups of theologians adapted the confession according to their theological convictions, producing the Savoy Declaration (1658) and the Second London Confession (1689). Thus the Westminster Confession is relevant to Presbyterians, Congregationalists, and Baptists. (xx) Why Another Commentary? The Westminster Confession has never lacked commentators. From the 17th century onward, pastors and theologians have written to explain its theology. Quality works by A. A. Hodge , G. I. Williamson, R. C. Sproul, and more recently Chad Van Dixhoorn have each served the church well in different ways. So why do we need another commentary on the confession, and what makes this one useful? The Westminster Confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. First, this isn’t the work of a single author but a collaborative effort by scholars whose expertise spans several areas of theology. That breadth allows the volume to approach the confession from different perspectives while maintaining a clear unity of purpose. Each contributor brings particular expertise to the section he addresses, but the volume as a whole is concerned with helping readers understand the confession and its significance for the church. Second, the commentary is consciously pastoral. Rath
articles.content_zh: 改革意味着什么? 标签经常使用,但并不总是谨慎。 对某些人来说,它只是提到救赎的特定观点. 对其他人来说,它引起一种传统、一种文化,甚至一种美学。 然而,从历史上看,改革意味着更加富有的东西。 虽然没有一句话能捕捉到被改造后的传统的全部,但至少它意味着三件事:是圣经,是盟约,是忏悔. 圣经的权威支配着我们的神学,盟约神学提供了圣经的红发框架,历史的忏悔总结并捍卫了教会的教义信念。 移除其中任何一根支柱,失去对改革后的传统至关重要的东西。 改革神学院长期试图在所有三个领域为牧师和教会成员提供教具, 近年来,该校院士编写了大量关于"旧约"和"新约"和"盟约神学"等著作. 现在,随着《威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和适用的综合评论》,他们把注意力转向改革后传统的忏悔基础。 结果的一卷不仅试图解释忏悔的教义,还试图表明为什么忏悔神学在今天仍然对教会至关重要. 韦斯敏斯特对信仰的忏悔是什么? 威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔会取而代之的是威斯敏斯特大会(Westminster Assembly),这是1643年英国议会在政治与教会剧变深刻的时期召开的由100多位部长和神学家组成的集会. 大会的任务是建议对英格兰教会的学说,崇拜,政府和纪律进行改革. 经过五年多的认真的圣经研究和神学审议后,大会产生了"威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)和"更大规模和更短的卡特克主义". 近四个世纪以来,这些文件共同成为全世界长老会教会的理论基础。 然而,议会的影响远远超出长老会。 忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架。 因此,它的神学影响塑造了几代基督教会,浸信会等福音派基督徒. 这本书的编辑们正确地指出,《忏悔书》也具有普世性,因为它在17世纪被基督教会和特定浸信会广泛接受,因为两个不同的神学家群体根据他们的神学信念修改了供词,产生了"萨伏依宣言"(1658年)和"第二次伦敦忏悔书"(1689年). 因此,威斯敏斯特忏悔与长老会、基督教会和浸信会有关。 (二十) 为什么另作一评注? 威斯敏斯特的"忏悔"从未缺少评论家. 从17世纪起,牧师和神学家都撰文解释其神学. A. A. Hodge、G. I. Williamson、R. C. Sproul和最近的Chad Van Dixhoorn以不同方式为教堂服务。 因此,我们为什么需要关于供词的另一条评论,是什么使得这一条有用呢? 威斯敏斯特忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架. 首先,这不是一位作者的工作,而是学者的合作努力,他们的专业知识跨越了神学的几个领域。 这种宽度允许量从不同的角度对待供词,同时保持明确的目的一致。 每个贡献者都会为他所讲的一节带来特殊的专门知识,但该卷整体关注的是帮助读者理解忏悔及其对教会的意义. 第二,评注是自觉的放肆。 拉斯语Name

articles.title: If the Church Did Its Job, Would the Parachurch Exist?
articles.summary: Do pregnancy centers, food pantries, or campus ministries exist because the church is failing to do her work?
articles.summary_zh: 是否存在怀孕中心、食品储藏室或校园事工，因为教会未能完成她的工作？
articles.title_zh: 如果教会做了它的工作，教堂会存在吗？
articles.content: I’ve heard it said more than once: “If the church did its job, the parachurch wouldn’t have to exist.” For instance, I was consulting with a local pastor who wanted to see the church serve people in poverty in his community. It was important to him that the church do it, not a nonprofit. Since he understood that God’s kingdom is bigger than his congregation, he wanted to engage multiple churches in the project. I suggested he consider forming a council of pastors and collectively hiring a staff member to manage the operations of the combined program. He thought that could work well for his context. I’m not sure he was aware of the irony. I certainly was: We’d just reinvented a variant of the 501(c)(3) nonprofit that he so keenly wanted to avoid in the first place. While the allergy to faith-based nonprofits was especially strong in his case, many people accept the premise at a basic level. In my experience, this sentiment is just as likely to come from someone who works in nonchurch ministry as from a pastor. If we understand the church is the core institution created by Christ to advance the kingdom of heaven, has it failed so badly that we need an army of auxiliaries to prop it up? Clarifying Terms and Roles I answer that the parachurch doesn’t exist because the church has failed. It exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. Proving that starts with clarifying terms. The parachurch exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. “Church” has more than one use in Scripture. In some contexts, it describes the people of God universally (Matt. 16:15–18; Eph. 1:22–23; Col. 1:18). In others, it’s a local congregational institution with the parameters God has placed around its operation (1 Thess. 1:1; 1 Tim. 3:1–5; Philem. 1:2; James 5:14). “Parachurch” typically refers to faith-based nonprofits who serve people in need or provide evangelistic and discipleship resources. Certainly, as part of the universal church, all God’s people hold equal status in advancing God’s mission, whether they labor as nurses, students, pastors, or tentmakers (see Acts 18:1–3). Just as surely, all God’s people shouldn’t merely attend but be accountable to a local congregation that enables their spiritual formation. When not assembled, God’s people are charged with many tasks—everything from stewarding creation to seeking justice for the oppressed. We can fulfill these tasks as individuals, but it often makes sense to create or join institutions dedicated to fulfilling them. Which brings us to a crucial point: God ordained some institutions specifically, and some emerged organically from God’s commands. Ordained or Emergent Institutions The family, the local church, and the government are ordained institutions. The Bible gives each ordained institution some guidance but also leaves a lot open to interpretation. While these ordained institutions are necessary for all people, they aren’t sufficient to fulfill God’s myriad commands to their fullest extent. Thus, some institutions emerge from the commands, rather than from a revealed institutional structure: The command to work led to the formation of businesses. The command to pass knowledge to subsequent generations led to the formation of schools. The command to care for the sick caused Christians to form the first hospitals. The command to care for the poor, widows, orphans, and strangers led to the formation of charities . The command to make disciples of all nations led to mission boards, publishing houses, and Bible-translation ministries. This ordained-emergent distinction parallels Abraham Kuyper’s “ sphere sovereignty ” in its recognition of institutions not explicitly outlined in Scripture. Many of these commands can be fulfilled to some lesser degree by the ordained institutions, but there are limitations. A family may work without forming a business, but they’ll never raise a skyscraper. Most be

articles.summary: Joel Beeke joins Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan to explore what the Puritans can teach today’s pastors about prayer, preaching, personal holiness, shepherding souls, handling criticism, and persevering in ministry.

articles.content: What can pastors today learn from the Puritans? Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan welcome Joel Beeke to discuss the lasting wisdom of Puritan pastors and theologians. Drawing from decades of studying and teaching the Puritans, Beeke explains why they placed such a high priority on prayer, personal holiness, and applying Scripture to the hearts and lives of their congregations. articles.title: On My Shelf: Life and Books with L. Michael Morales
articles.summary: L. Michael Morales talks about what’s on his bedside table, favorite fiction, favorite rereads, and more.
articles.summary_zh: L. Michael Morales谈论他床头柜上的东西、最喜欢的小说、最喜欢的重读等等。
articles.title_zh: 在我的架子上： L. Michael Morales的生活和书籍
articles.content: On My Shelf helps you get to know various writers through a behind-the-scenes glimpse into their lives as readers. I asked L. Michael Morales—professor at Greenville Presbyterian Theological Seminary and author of Exodus Old and New: A Biblical Theology of Redemption —about what’s on his bedside table, his favorite fiction, the books he regularly revisits, and more. What’s on your nightstand right now? Malcolm Guite’s Galahad and the Grail . Myths of origin hold potential for shaping a society’s culture and character. I believe Guite, aside from writing good poetry and a national epic, is endeavoring to reawaken (or refound) England to her rich Christian heritage. This volume is the first of a projected four-volume work that may well represent the new definitive collection of Arthurian legends. Writings of the Ramban , translated and annotated by Charles B. Chavel. Nachmanides is my favorite medieval Jewish exegete and commentator, and these essays illumine his character and offer gleaming gems of insight. His essay on redemption, for example, gives a nuanced understanding of eschatology in the Hebrew Scriptures. He argues convincingly that the exile threatened in Leviticus relates to the Babylonian exile that occurred in Jeremiah’s day, whereas exile in Deuteronomy uses more eschatological language and seems to relate to the exile after the Second Temple’s destruction. Another essay records his Disputation in Barcelona, when Nachmanides was forced by the Spanish government to engage in debate with a Jewish Christian convert. The disputation eventually led to his exile from Spain since, as one of the intellectual giants of his era, he acquitted himself overly well. (Christian readers will, for the most part, be disappointed with the representation of our faith by his opponent, but the disputation is helpful in that it offers insights into the sort of questions about the Messiah we should think about more deeply.) What are your favorite fiction books? Aside from literary classics, I enjoy mystery books, especially medieval mysteries, although it’s hard to find good ones. Ellis Peters’s Brother Cadfael series is good, although aimed for a younger audience (and so a bit tame). She had a beautifully poetic sense of providence and justice, which makes for satisfying conclusions. I also appreciate the espionage genre, such as the early works of John le Carré, like The Spy Who Came in from the Cold , A Small Town in Germany , and Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy . Perhaps less thoughtful but often more fun, Alistair MacLean’s books never fail to offer a little escape into adventure. What biographies or autobiographies have most influenced you and why? Iain H. Murray’s two-volume biography of D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones had a profound impact on me as a young, inexperienced pastor—my copies are filled with underlining and scribbled notes. This account of the Doctor’s life and ministry not only led me onto the paths of the Reformed faith, but demonstrated God’s blessings on a faithful minister’s diligent commitment to the ordinary means of grace, to prayer and preaching. Many of the problems and challenges facing the wider evangelical church when I was pastoring had their roots in the era of Lloyd-Jones’s ministry, so reading his biography offered much-needed biblical wisdom and the discernment of hindsight. Augustine’s Confessions is also a treasured book—it’s so personal and honest, and displays the sure and gracious hand of God in one’s life. Confessions is also about Augustine’s mother, Monica, and how she persevered in prayer on his behalf; and about God’s faithfulness and goodness in answering her prayers so abundantly. Throughout the book, readers also get fascinating glimpses of life in the late fourth and early fifth centuries. What are some books you regularly reread and why? Aside from regular Bible reading, it’s a challenge to reread many books, since my research-reading stacks are always waiting. Classics and modern classics, however
articles.content_zh: 《我的书架》帮助你了解各种作家, 通过幕后人物的一幕来了解他们作为读者的生活。 我问L. Michael Morales — — 格林维尔长老会神学院的教授和《出老而新:救赎的圣经神学》的作者 — — 关于他的床边桌子上的内容、他最喜欢的虚构故事、他经常重读的书籍等等。 现在睡台上有什么? 马尔科姆·盖特的加拉哈德和圣杯。 起源神话具有塑造社会文化和性格的潜力。 我相信Guite除了写好诗作和国史诗外,还努力使英国重新认识(或重新发现)她丰富的基督教遗产。 本卷是一出预测的四卷作品中的第一部,很可能代表了"亚瑟传奇"的新最终集. 由Charles B. Chavel翻译和注释的《拉姆班人》的著作。 纳克曼尼得斯是我最喜欢的中世纪犹太人的特质和评论家,这些散文照亮了他的性格,并提供了光辉的洞察力. 例如,他关于赎罪的论文对希伯来圣经中的空想学有细微的理解. 他令人信服地辩称,在利维提库斯受到的放逐与耶利米时代发生的巴比伦人放逐有关,而Deuteronomy的放逐则使用更多的宗教语言,似乎与第二圣殿被摧毁之后的放逐有关。 另一篇散文记录了他在巴塞罗那的争议,当时纳克曼尼得斯被西班牙政府强迫与一名犹太基督徒皈依者展开辩论. 争议最终导致他被流放出西班牙,因为作为他时代的知识巨头之一,他为自己释出过好. (基督教读者大多会对其对手代表我们的信仰感到失望,但争论很有帮助,因为它能让人们深入了解我们应该更深入地思考的弥赛亚问题。 ) 你最喜欢什么小说? 除了文学经典之外,我还喜欢神秘的书籍,特别是中世纪的神秘,尽管很难找到好的书籍。 Ellis Peters的"Cadfael兄弟"系列虽然针对年轻观众(也有点温柔), 她有着美妙的诗意感 天赐和正义, 这可以得出令人满意的结论。 我也欣赏间谍流派,如约翰·勒·卡雷的早期作品,如"从寒冷中进来的间谍"(The Spy Who Came in from the Cold),"德国的一个小镇"(A Small Town)和"丁克"(Tinker,裁缝,Soldier,Spy)等. Alistair MacLean的书中, 什么传记或自传 影响最大,为什么? Iain H. Murray的两卷自传D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones对我这个年轻、经验不足的牧师产生了深远的影响——我的书中充满了强调和写作的笔记。 这种对医生生活和牧师的描述不仅使我走上了改革后信仰的道路,而且表明上帝保佑一位忠实的大臣勤勉地致力于普通的恩典、祈祷和传道。 在我做牧师时,广大福音派教会所面临的许多问题和挑战都起源于劳埃德-琼斯部的时代,因此阅读他的传记提供了急需的圣经智慧和后视力。 奥古斯丁的忏悔书也是一本珍贵的书 -- -- 它非常个人和诚实,在一个人的生活中展现出上帝的坚定和仁慈之手。 忏悔的内容还包括奥古斯丁的母亲莫妮卡,以及她如何代表他坚持祈祷;以及上帝如此忠实和善良地回答她的祈祷。 在整个书中,读者也获得了第四世纪后期和第五世纪初生活的迷人一瞥. 你经常读什么书? 除了定期阅读圣经之外, 重读许多书籍也是个挑战, 然而,古典和现代古典

articles.title: How Can I Find the Motivation to Use My Time Better at Work?
articles.summary: Let’s start by counting the cost.
articles.summary_zh: 让我们从计算成本开始。
articles.title_zh: 如何找到更好地利用工作时间的动力？
articles.content: I work for a property management company that oversees retail space. I haven’t been doing this very long, but I’m finding that I’m not as productive as I’d like to be. Often, entertainment and fear of failure keep me from working. How can I get motivated to use my time better? Given that we’re to submit to our earthly masters with sincere hearts as unto Christ (Eph. 6:5), our productivity at work isn’t ultimately about our advancement or our employer’s success—it’s about our gospel witness. From before the fall, God ordained our work for keeping, cultivating, subduing, and exercising dominion over his creation. We’re still called to that today in any work to which we set our hand—including the property management of retail space. As believers, all work invites us to leverage our God-given talents and strength to bless and bring order to God’s creation in order to glorify him. When alluring distractions or a fear of failure hinder our labor, we can turn to him who calls us for the truth that will rightly spur us on. Distraction of Entertainment When entertainment distracts us from working, we should start by counting the cost. If we’re spending work hours on entertainment and then have to finish our tasks in what should be our free time, what else is this keeping us from stewarding well? It may be infringing on our time for relationships, spiritual disciplines, or true rest. On the other hand, if our working hours are fixed regardless of how on (or off) task we are, such as a job we clock in and out of with responsibilities only while we’re present, why are we willing to steal from our employer by accepting their payment without exchanging it for the labor we promised? Maybe we need to “cut off” what’s tempting us by blocking entertainment apps on our phone and computer during the workday (Matt. 5:30). If we’re spending work hours on entertainment, what else is this keeping us from stewarding well? Once we do, how might we instead faithfully devote that time to our employer’s good, even being willing to go a mile beyond what’s expected of us (v. 41)? Maybe we provide the talking points requested for a presentation—but also organize them into slides to save someone else from having to do so. Maybe we address the three issues our leader ask us to correct—but also address two more we discovered in the process. Perhaps if we worked with this level of diligence and care, like Joseph with Potiphar, we’d be given increased responsibility and influence that could be leveraged for the kingdom. Those who can be trusted with little can also be trusted with much (Gen. 39:1–6; Luke 16:10). Certainly, God would be glorified as we work with all our heart as to the Lord and not to man (Col. 3:23). Fear of Failure When a fear of failure keeps us from working altogether, we can start by digging out the root of that fear. Do you fear that your limitations and propensity to error will keep you from succeeding? Acknowledge that inaction guarantees you won’t succeed, but attempts to succeed in the work God has entrusted to you allow the opportunity for his power to be made perfect in your weakness (2 Cor. 12:9). When you feel discouraged by your insufficiencies, trust God to provide the wisdom and strength necessary for the work to which he’s called you—by prayer (James 1:5), the edification of his Word, and your humble pursuit of correction and growth through helpful resources and the example of others. Do you fear others’ judgment when you fail? Remember that your purpose is ultimately to please God, not man, and that there’s no condemnation for those in Christ (Rom. 8:1; Gal. 1:10). When you make a mistake or fall short of what’s expected of you, admit your error, seek understanding about what to do differently, and move forward with the humility and resolve that may make others respect you even more than they did before. articles.content_zh: 我为一家监管零售空间的物业管理公司工作 但我发现自己没有自己想要的那么有生产力。 通常,娱乐和对失败的恐惧使我无法工作. 我怎么能有积极性 更好地利用我的时间? 我们的工作效率最终不是关于我们的进步或雇主的成功, 而是关于我们的福音见证。 从秋天之前开始,上帝就规定我们的工作是保持、培育、征服和支配他的创造。 包括零售空间的物业管理。 作为信徒,一切工作都邀请我们利用上帝赐予我们的才华和力量来祝福并给上帝的创造带来秩序来赞美他. 当引人注意或担心失败会阻碍我们的工作时,我们可以求助于他,他呼唤我们寻求正确激励我们的事实。 娱乐的分心 当娱乐干扰我们工作时,我们应该从计算成本入手。 如果我们在娱乐上花工时, 然后必须在什么是空闲时间完成我们的任务, 它可能侵犯我们的时间 关系,精神学科,或真正的休息。 另一方面,如果我们的工作时间是固定的,不管我们是如何完成(或关闭)任务的,比如我们只是在在场时就负责地工作,那么我们为什么愿意接受雇主的付款而不以我们承诺的劳动来换取呢? 也许我们需要在工作日(Matt. 如果我们在娱乐上花工时, 一旦我们这样做了,我们如何忠实地把时间用于雇主的利益,甚至愿意超越我们的期望(v.41)? 也许我们提供了演讲所要求的谈话要点,但也把它们组织成幻灯片,以拯救别人不必这样做。 我们或许可以解决我们领导人要求我们纠正的三个问题, 也许如果我们像约瑟夫和波提乏那样勤奋谨慎, 能够被很少信任的人也可以被很多信任(Gen. 39:1-6;Luke 16:10). 当然,当我们全心全意地为主而不是为人工作时,上帝将受到赞美(第3:23上校)。 对失败的恐惧 当对失败的恐惧使我们无法完全工作时,我们可以首先挖掘出这种恐惧的根源。 难道你怕自己的限制和偏执使你无法成功吗? 承认这种无所作为保证了你不会成功,但为了在上帝委托给你的工作上取得成功而作的尝试,允许他的机会在你的弱点中完美地发挥出他的力量(2 Cor. 12:9). 当你们因自己的不足而感到沮丧时,请相信上帝为他所说的你们的工作提供必要的智慧和力量——通过祈祷(詹姆斯1:5),将他的话化,并通过有益的资源和他人的榜样谦卑地追求纠正和成长。 难道你不怕别人的判断吗? 记住你的目的最终是为了取悦上帝,而不是取悦人类,对基督中的人没有谴责(8:1;Gal:1:10). 当你们犯错误或者没有达到预期时,你们承认自己的错误,寻求了解应该如何采取不同的做法,并以谦卑和决心前进,这可能会使别人比以前更加尊重你们。 相信上帝为他所说的你的工作提供必要的智慧和力量。 你怕你的身份吗?

articles.title: Simon Says: Inconspicuous Evidence of Eyewitnesses in Mark
articles.summary: Several features indicate that the eyewitness accounts of Simon stand behind Mark’s Gospel.
articles.summary_zh: 有几个特征表明，西门的目击者叙述支持马可福音。
articles.title_zh: 西蒙说：马可福音中不明显的目击者证据
articles.content: When I watch Jesus films, whether the current series The Chosen , The Passion of the Christ in the early 2000s , or even Godspell from the 1970s, I can’t help but ask, Where did they get those stories? Sometimes I can piece together bits from Matthew, Mark, Luke, or John. Occasionally I detect legendary material from church history or the apocryphal gospels. But at other times, my best guess is “They made it up,” and I ascribe the scene to creative liberty. When we turn to the Gospel of Mark, which most scholars see as the first extant telling of the story of Jesus, we might also wonder, Where did Mark get these stories? Around the 1920s to ’50s, the fashionable scholarly answer was found in a field of study known as form criticism . This enterprise tried to tie different sayings and stories of Jesus back to an occasion within the early church that would have prompted their creation. Though the heyday of form criticism has passed, the legacy of seeing the Gospels as a “mixtape” of various ad hoc literary traditions can still be seen today. In contrast to form criticism and the Jesus-film industry, the canonical Gospels are sourced in eye-witness testimony and were written within living memory of the events they describe. Perhaps no other scholar has written so persuasively on this subject as Richard Bauckham in his magisterial Jesus and the Eyewitnesses . Indications of eye-witness testimony are peppered throughout Mark’s gospel. Here we will consider just a few, each revolving around the name “Simon.” These are more obscure than what normally make their way into works on apologetics, but their subtlety is a strength since they are not the kind of details one fabricates. We will discover that inconspicuous indicators of eyewitnesses reveal what is happening behind the scenes more than front-and-center observations. Evidence of Simon Peter There are signs that Simon Peter has been a significant source for Mark’s Gospel, despite Mark not making a show of it. The church father Papias famously stated that Mark was Peter’s interpreter, who wrote down what he remembered from his preaching. Though many scholars doubt Papias here, Mark goes out of his way to emphasize Simon Peter. Several features indicate that Mark is particularly told from a Petrine perspective. For example, his prominence verges on redundancy when he is introduced in 1:16: “Passing alongside the Sea of Galilee, [Jesus] saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.” This is part of what Bauckham calls a Peter inclusio, so that his testimony brackets the Gospel of Mark (see 16:7). Later in the narrative, those “sick or oppressed by demons” are brought to Jesus in Capernaum (1:32), the summary after the climactic exorcism at the synagogue (vv. 21–28). But sandwiched in the middle is the healing of Simon’s mother-in-law (vv. 29–31). Similarly, Mark writes of when the disciples look for Jesus, “Simon and those who were with him searched for him” (v. 36). Details like these betray a “Simon-centric” source. Bauckham argues that, with few exceptions, “Peter is actually present through a large proportion of the narrative from 1:16 to 14:72.” Several features indicate that Mark is particularly told from a Petrine perspective. An oddity in Mark’s grammatical style reinforces not just Simon Peter’s perspective but that of all the disciples: Mark uniquely favors using plural verbs to introduce singular ones. For example, Mark 11:12 reads, “On the following day, when they came from Bethany, he [Jesus] was hungry” (emphasis added). This provides the perspective of the group, as opposed to Matthew’s retelling: “In the morning, as he was returning to the city, he became hungry” (21:18). This literary device occurs 21 times in Mark’s narrative. Evidence of Many Simons The name “Simon” occurs 11 times in Mark. It most famously refers to Peter (1:16 [twice], 29, 30, 36; 3:16; 14:37), but it also refers to the other apostle, “Simon the Z
articles.content_zh: 当我看耶稣的电影时,无论是现在的系列"选择"(The Chosen, The Passion of the Christ in 20世纪20年代早期),还是甚至从20世纪70年代起的"神话"(Godspell),我都不得不问,他们从哪里得到这些故事的? 有时我可以拼凑出马修,马克,卢克或约翰的位子. 偶尔我也会从教堂历史或启示录中 发现传奇材料 但在其他时候,我的最佳猜测是“他们编造的”,我把场景描述为创造性的自由。 当我们转向"马克福音"时,大多数学者认为它是第一个讲述耶稣故事的现存者,我们也可能会想,"马克从哪里得到这些故事的? 20世纪20至50年代, 时髦的学术答案出现在一个研究领域, 这个事业试图把耶稣的不同说法和故事与早期教会内部本来会促使他们创造的机会联系起来. 尽管形式批评的热潮已经过去,但今天仍然可以看到将福音书视为各种临时文学传统“混合”的遗产。 与形而上学的批评和耶稣-电影行业形成对比的是,"神舟福音"来源于目击证人的证词并被写在了他们描述的事件活生生的记忆中. 可能没有其他学者如此有说服力地写了 理查德·鲍克汉姆 在他的大法官耶稣和目击证人。 在马克的福音中, 在这里,我们将只考虑几个,每个环绕“西蒙”的名称。 这些比平时在古琴系上的工作更为模糊,但是其微妙性是一种力量,因为它们不是一种编织出来的细节。 我们将发现,目击证人的不显眼指标显示在幕后发生的情况比前中观察更明显。 西蒙·彼得的证据 有迹象表明西蒙·彼得一直是"马克福音"的重要出处,尽管马克没有对此表态. 教父帕皮亚斯出名地说,马克是彼得的翻译,他记下了他在布道时所记得的. 虽然许多学者怀疑这里有帕皮阿斯,但马克却不择手段地强调西蒙·彼得. 一些特征表明,马克尤其被从Petrine的角度讲述. 例如,在1:16介绍他时,他的突出之处是冗余:“[耶稣]在加利利海一并看到西蒙的兄弟西蒙和安德鲁将网投入大海,因为他们是渔民。” 这是Bauckham称之为"彼得·因克利奥"的一部分,因此他的证词将马克福音(见16:7)置于其中. 后来在叙事中,那些"被恶魔所生病或被压迫"的人被带到了卡佩尔瑙姆的耶稣面前(1:32),即犹太会堂的高潮驱魔后的摘要(v. 21–28). 但中间的三明治是西蒙婆婆(vv. 29–31)的治愈. 同样地,马克写道,当门徒们寻找耶稣时,“西蒙和与他在一起的人寻找他”(v.36)。 这些细节背叛了“以西蒙为中心”的来源。 Bauckham认为,除了少数例外,“彼得实际上通过1:16至14:72的很大一部分叙述存在。” 一些特征表明,马克尤其被从Petrine的角度讲述. 马克语法风格的奇特之处不仅强化了西蒙·彼得的观点,而且强化了所有门徒的观点: 使用复数动词标记独有的偏好来引入单数。 例如,Mark 11:12写道:“第二天,当他们从Bethany来时,他[耶稣]饿了”(着重号由作者标明)。 这提供了这个团体的视角,而不是马修的重述:"早上,当他回到城市时,他变得饥饿"(21:18). 这个文学装置在马克的叙述中发生21次. 许多西蒙的证据 “西蒙”这个名字在马克有11次出现。 最出名的是彼得(1:16 [两次],29,30,36;3:16;14:37),但也指另一位使徒"Simon the Z".
articles.author: Bruce Henning

articles.title: Broken Bodies Make Beautiful Temples
articles.summary: We must view our foreign-feeling bodies as vessels through which God demonstrates his redeeming strength.
articles.summary_zh: 我们必须把外在的身体看作是神展示祂救赎力量的器皿。
articles.title_zh: 破碎的身体造就美丽的寺庙
articles.content: The Lord’s ways are not our ways (Isa. 55:8–9). Do we take this seriously, or do we revert to “our ways” in desperate seasons when we wander from God to seek meaning? I revisit this battle every time I look in the mirror at a quadriplegic body I desperately hope is not me. “Our ways” tell me that the body is incidental to identity. It’s an enticing lie that exploits disorienting bodily experiences such as disability , sickness, gender dysphoria, or other bodily insecurities hindering people from seeing meaning in bodies that feel foreign. I don’t see the nobility of God’s image or a temple worthy to house the divine when I’m being catheterized, bathed, or rolled in bed to prevent pressure sores. For others, disfiguration, tumors, or injury characterize bodies they can’t wait to “escape” at the second coming. For still others, their bodies contradict strong inward feelings telling them who they “really” are. Whatever the motivation, we tend to downplay bodily meaning when we feel it compromises our dignity. But this is autonomy’s way, not the Lord’s way. Scripture tells us there’s nothing undignified about weak, broken, dependent, or foreign-feeling bodies. The apostle Paul says our bodies (of all conditions) are temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 6:19). No higher calling exists for the physical than to serve as a temple to house its Creator. Paul’s claim is a hard truth for those with bodily insecurities, because it means we must trade the disdain we feel toward our bodies for contentment—a difficult but worthy exchange. ‘Glory of the Immortal God’ Paul is well acquainted with bodily fragility and limitations, yet he doesn’t hesitate to make the body central to the identity of people he calls “more than conquerors through him who loved us” (Rom. 8:37). For example, Paul observes in Romans 1:18–31 that the quintessential sin resulting from “exchang[ing] the truth about God for a lie” (v. 25) and “exchang[ing] the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man” (v. 23) is bodily sin that distorts God’s “very good” design for the body (Gen. 1:31). Thus, the “glory of the immortal God” of which Paul speaks is, at least in part, our bodies, which God created as his image (vv. 26–27). In Romans 6, Paul includes the body as part of the life Christ calls us to after “we have died with Christ” and subsequently “also live with him” (v. 8). He exhorts us to use our bodies “as instruments for righteousness” (vv. 12–13). Paul makes no exception for those with bodily insecurities. The body God gave you is an instrument for righteousness, no matter how broken or “inauthentic” it may feel. God’s Image, Not Ours Scripture teaches that my bodily self, no matter how foreign it feels, is me . And, like the rest of me, it doesn’t “belong” to me for two reasons. First, we’re not our own because the Lord makes his temples. Under the new covenant, “the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands” (Acts 7:48), and the “Lord of heaven . . . does not live in temples made by man” (17:24). I did not make myself. The Lord “fearfully and wonderfully made” me; I am his “wonderful” work (Ps. 139:14) and “workmanship” (Eph. 2:10). He “formed my inward parts” and “knitted me together” (Ps. 139:13). Even brokenness, including disability, is the Lord’s wonderful work (Ex. 4:11; John 9:2–4). Second, we’re not our own because the Lord purchased us, body and all. Paul tells us bluntly, “You were bought with a price” (1 Cor. 6:20). A very high price: the death of his Son. My body is his, disability and all. Nothing about me is “mine” to do with as I please. My body is a temple for the Lord , not for me. He designed, constructed, and purposed it. “I” am no longer my own. Rather, my body is “meant . . . for the Lord, and the Lord for [my] body” (1 Cor. 6:13). My body is his, disability and all. Nothing about me is ‘mine’ to do with as I please. God has purposed my broken body and purchased my identity at the great price of his Son’s death to proclaim h
articles.content_zh: 主道不是我们的道(以萨. 55:8-9). 我们是否认真对待这个问题,还是在绝望的季节里,当我们从上帝那里徘徊去寻求意义时,我们又回到“我们的方式”上来? 每次我照镜子时,我都会重温这场战斗,我迫切地希望这不是我。 “我们的方法”告诉我,尸体是身份的附带因素。 利用残疾、疾病、性别障碍或其他不安全感等令人不快的身体体验, 我看不到上帝的尊贵形象, 对其他人来说, 对其他人来说,他们的身体与告诉他们自己“真正”是谁的强烈内在感情相矛盾。 无论动机为何,当我们觉得身体损害我们的尊严时,我们往往会贬低身体意义。 但这是自治的方式,不是主的方式。 圣经告诉我们,对于软弱、破碎、依附或异国情调的躯体,没有什么不光彩的。 使徒保罗说,我们的身体(所有条件)都是圣灵的圣殿(1 Cor. 6:19). 没有比作为寺庙容纳造物主更高的要求了。 保罗的主张对身体不安全感的人来说是很难接受的,因为这意味着我们必须用我们对身体的蔑视来换取满足感——一种艰难而有价值的交换。 保罗非常熟悉身体的脆弱性和局限性,但他毫不犹豫地将身体置于他所称的“比通过爱我们的人来征服者”的人身份的中心地位(第8:37室)。 例如,保罗在罗马语1:18-31中观察到, " 以谎言为由推翻上帝的真理 " (v. 25)和 " 以不朽之神的光荣为像凡人的形象 " (v. 23)所产生的五等罪是身体罪,扭曲了上帝对身体的 " 非常好 " 的设计(Gen. 1:31)。 因此,保罗所说的“不朽之神的荣耀”至少部分是我们的身体,上帝创造了我们的身体作为其形象(v. 26-27)。 在罗马人6中,保罗将尸体列为基督要求我们在“与基督同生共死”之后生活的一部分,随后又“与他同生共活”(v.8)。 他劝我们用我们的身体 " 作为正义的工具 " (v.v.12-13)。 保罗对身体不安全的人也不例外。 上帝赐予你的身体是正义的工具,无论它多么破碎或“不真实”的感觉如何。 上帝的影像,而不是我们的经典,教导我身体的自我,无论感觉多么外在,都是我。 与我其他人一样, 我们不是自己人, 根据新盟约,“最高层不居住在由手造的房屋”(第7:48号法)和“天主......不居住在由人造的寺庙”(17:24)。 我没有做我自己。 主“亲切而出色地”我;我是他“出色”的作品(第139:14页)和“工作技巧”(第2:10页)。 他“组成了我的内在部分”并“把我织在一起”(第139:13页)。 甚至包括残疾在内的骨折也是主的精彩作品(Ex. 4:11;John 9:2–4). 我们不是自己人, 保罗直言不讳地告诉我们,“你被买下的价格”(第6:20节)。 一个非常高的代价:他儿子的死. 我的身体是他的,残疾和所有。 与我无关, 我的身体是上帝的神庙,不是我 他设计、建造和设计它。 “我”不再是我自己。 相反,我的身体是“为主而出,为我而出"(第6:13节)。 我的身体是他的,残疾和所有。 与我无关, 上帝用我破碎的躯体 以他儿子死后的巨大代价买下我的身份

articles.title: What My Grandparents Taught Me About Pastoral Ministry
articles.summary: You’re being prepared for the work the Lord has for you in ways you may not understand until you’re standing in a hospice living room.
articles.summary_zh: 你正准备好接受主为你所做的工作，直到你站在临终关怀的客厅里，你才会明白。
articles.title_zh: 关于牧灵事工，我的祖父母教会了我什么
articles.content: When I was in high school, and early on during the summers in college, I spent my days working at a local pharmacy. I got a one-hour lunch break, and I ended up going almost every day to lunch at my favorite place: Granny and PawPaw’s house. I don’t remember how it started. One day, I drove over on my lunch break, and after that, it became my routine. They wanted to see me, and I wanted to see them. Sitting at their table instead of alone at a restaurant was comfortable and unhurried. At the time, I didn’t think much about it. I was just eating lunch with my grandparents. But looking back, I realize the Lord was doing more than I understood. Having now sat beside countless hospital beds and in living rooms with families walking through suffering, I can see how those lunches prepared me for ministry in ways I didn’t yet understand. My grandparents taught me how to slow down, listen, and simply be present with people. PawPaw When we ate, my grandfather talked mostly about his time serving in the Korean War, his years as an insurance agent for Liberty National, or fishing, which he loved almost as much as anything in the world. Courtesy Jared Cornutt Of the three topics, he talked about Korea the most. The war had ended decades earlier, but it hadn’t really ended for him. It shaped the rest of his life. PawPaw survived the war; he never escaped it. He talked around it in the way men of his generation often did when they carried wounds no one had given them language for. They wanted to see me, and I wanted to see them. At the time, I didn’t think much about it. I was just eating lunch with my grandparents. When I sat across from him at that table, I didn’t know what PTSD was. I just knew Korea was never far from his mind. Now I realize why. My PawPaw came home from the war during an era when PTSD wasn’t understood. Men like him were told to put the war behind them. They were expected to come home, go to work, raise a family, and move on. Many did. But many, like my grandfather, carried the war with them for the rest of their lives. As a boy, I didn’t understand that. I just knew him first as my grandfather, and I knew he loved me. I’m thankful that’s how I got to know him. Granny My grandmother had an tenth-grade education. She grew up on a farm in a poverty she also never fully escaped. She never had much of a formal education, but I can tell you this: She knew the Lord, and the Lord knew her. If you heard her whole story, you might call her life a tragedy. But due to her remarkable faith, she wouldn’t describe it that way. Courtesy Jared Cornutt I can still see her sitting in that rocking chair when I’d come over, reading glasses on and her Bible open in her lap. She was eager to tell me what she’d read that morning. She loved God’s Word because she needed it and depended on it. Every time I left her house, she’d tell me the same thing: “I’m praying for you.” That meant more to me than any gift she could’ve ever given, because I knew she wasn’t just saying it. She really was praying for me . I now know there was much about her life I didn’t understand. But what stayed with me was that my grandmother loved Jesus, loved his Word, and faithfully prayed for her grandson. The Lord didn’t answer every prayer she prayed the way she hoped. But I’ve often wondered how many of God’s kindnesses in my life came through Granny’s faithful prayers. Ministry Now I share all this because I recently sat in another living room. It was different, but it felt oddly familiar. As I left that room, it dawned on me almost immediately that I was equipped to minister there only because of those lunches years before. Every time I left her house, she’d tell me the same thing: ‘I’m praying for you.’ That meant more to me than any gift she could’ve ever given. I visited a member of my church, a woman in her 80s, who has leukemia. The infusions aren’t working. Neither are the other treatments. Her doctor has told her, in words kind but final, to go home and ma
articles.content_zh: 高中时,大学暑期初期,我在当地一家药店工作了好几天. 我有一个一小时的午餐休息, 我几乎每天都去我最喜欢的地方吃午饭:奶奶和PawPaw的房子。 我不记得它是如何开始的。 有一天,我开车过来 在我的午餐休息, 之后,它成为我的常规。 他们想见我 我想见他们 坐在他们的桌子上,而不是独自在一家餐馆,是舒适而无所事事的. 我当时没有怎么考虑。 我只是和我外祖父母吃午饭 但回头看,我意识到上帝做的比我想象的还要多. 现在坐在无数的医院病床旁边, 我的外祖父母教我如何慢下来,倾听,并且只是和人们在一起。 aw 我们吃饭时,我祖父主要谈到他在朝鲜战争中服役的时间,他作为自由国民保险代理人的岁月,或者钓鱼的时间,他喜欢钓鱼的时间几乎和世界上的一切一样多. 敬礼雅里德·科努特 在三个话题中,他谈论韩国最多. 战争于几十年前结束, 它塑造了他的余生。 PawPaw在战争中幸存;他从未逃脱. 他用他这一代人的方式谈论这个问题,当他们背负着没有人给他们任何语言的创伤时,他们经常这样做。 他们想见我 我想见他们 我当时没有怎么考虑。 我只是和我外祖父母吃午饭 我坐在他对面, 我只知道韩国从不离他远 现在我明白了为什么。 我的PawPaw是战争结束后回家的, 他这样的人被告知要放弃战争 他们应该回家,去工作,养活一个家庭,然后继续前进。 很多人都这样 但是,许多人,像我祖父一样,在他们的余生中与他们一起背负着战争. 作为一个男孩,我不明白这一点。 我以祖父的身份认识他 我知道他爱我 我很感激, 外婆 外婆 外婆 外婆 我祖母受过十年级的教育 她在一个贫困的农场里长大 也从未完全逃脱过 她从来没有受过很多正规教育,但我可以告诉你:她认识主,而主认识她. 如果你听到她的整个故事, 你可能会说她的生活是悲剧。 她不会这样描述。 我仍能看到她坐在摇椅上, 她急于告诉我当天早上读了什么。 她喜欢上帝的话,因为她需要并且依赖上帝的话。 每次我离开她家,她都会告诉我同样的事情:“我在为你祈祷。 ” 这对我来说比她所赐的任何礼物都重要, 她真的为我祈祷 现在我知道她的生活有很多我不明白的事。 但留在我身边的是,我祖母爱耶稣,爱他的话语,并忠诚地为她孙子祈祷. 主没有按她所希望的方式, 但我常常想知道, 有多少上帝的慈悲通过奶奶的忠实祈祷而降临。 现在,我分享这一切 因为我最近坐在另一个客厅。 不一样,但感觉很熟悉 当我离开那间屋子时,我几乎立刻意识到,我之所以能够在那里担任部长,只是因为几年前的午餐。 每次我离开她家,她都会告诉我同样的事情:‘我在为你祈祷. 这对我来说比她所赐的任何礼物都重要。 我拜访了我教会的一位成员 一个80多岁的女性 她得了白血病 输液无效。 其他治疗方法也一样。 她的医生已经告诉她,用言语 善良但最终,回家和妈妈

articles.title: Hope in a Hero
articles.summary: In a film about a vigilante crime-fighting hero, the protagonist seems to be waging an impossible war. Not only is his city overrun with violence and theft, but he also discovers that the police force, court system, and public officials are corrupt. He’s repeatedly tempted to give up on the city and leave.
articles.summary_zh: 在一部关于义警打击犯罪英雄的电影中，主角似乎正在发动一场不可能的战争。他的城市不仅充斥着暴力和盗窃，而且他还发现警察部队、法院系统和公职人员腐败。他一再想放弃这座城市而离开。

articles.title: A Rich Life of Gratitude
articles.summary: In a letter dated September 13, 1943—five months after his imprisonment for opposing the Nazi regime—Dietrich Bonhoeffer wrote his parents. He asked for books and paper. He thanked them for the ways they’d helped him, and said, “It’s a strange feeling to be so completely dependent on other people; but at least it teaches one to be grateful, and I hope I shall never forget that.
articles.summary_zh: 在他因反对纳粹政权而被监禁五个月后的1943年9月13日的一封信中，迪特里希·朋霍费尔写信给他的父母。他要书和纸。他感谢他们帮助他的方式，并说： “完全依赖他人是一种奇怪的感觉；但至少它教会了我要感恩，我希望我永远不会忘记这一点。

articles.summary: One particularly catchy book promotion featured the auctioning of the chance for readers to have their name in print. Willing participants could pay to have their names used for a character in a bestselling author’s upcoming novel. The highest bidder in the auction won a chance to select a name to be used in the book.

articles.summary: The British TV reality show Portrait Artist of the Year pits nine amateur painters against each other in creating portraits of a local celebrity. The images have to be completed in just four hours, which is condensed into the one-hour program. It’s fascinating to watch the cameras capture each artist’s creation slowly emerging from a blank canvas.
articles.summary_zh: 这位英国电视真人秀年度肖像艺术家让九位业余画家互相对立，为当地名人创作肖像。这些图像必须在短短四个小时内完成，并浓缩成一小时的节目。观看相机捕捉每位艺术家从空白画布上慢慢浮现的创作，令人着迷。

articles.title: Carried Through
articles.summary: Lillie Cunningham is 110 years old, yet she isn’t reliant on a cane or walker. She does rely on Scripture, however, which she reads every morning and night—and attends church every Sunday. When she considers her life, she states, “I just always had faith and trust in God that he was going to carry us through.”
articles.summary_zh: Lillie Cunningham已经110岁了，但她并不依赖拐杖或助行器。然而，她确实依靠每天早上和晚上读的经文，并且每个星期天都去教堂。当她考虑自己的生活时，她说： “我一直对上帝有信心和信任，相信他会带领我们度过难关。”

articles.title: Grace in Grief
articles.summary: The world watched the news in horror as the sightseeing helicopter flying over the river tore into pieces. As the main rotor and tail broke off, the cabin plunged into the waters below, with the pilot and a family of five trapped inside. Just days after the tragedy that had taken the lives of his sister, brother-in-law, niece, and two nephews, the brother was at the site honoring his loved ones.
articles.summary_zh: 世界惊恐地看着这条消息，观光直升机飞过河面撕成碎片。随着主旋翼和尾翼脱落，机舱陷入了下面的水域，飞行员和一个五口之家被困在里面。在夺走他姐姐、姐夫、侄女和两个侄子生命的悲剧发生几天后，这位兄弟就在现场纪念他的亲人。

articles.title: Why the Doctrine of Conversion Matters for Membership Interviews
articles.summary: It’s difficult to discern whether someone has been converted if you’re hazy on what conversion is.   The post  Why the Doctrine of Conversion Matters for Membership Interviews  appeared first on  9Marks .
articles.summary_zh: 如果你不知道什么是皈依，就很难辨别某人是否已经皈依。帖子Why the Doctrine of Conversion Matters for Membership Interviews首次出现在9Marks上。
articles.title_zh: 为什么转换原则对会员面试很重要
articles.content: Abstract: David Burnette explains why the doctrine of conversion is so crucial for pastors and churches as they carry out their responsibilities in affirming new members as believers. We must not only understand what conversion is but also be able to apply it to the lives of real people. After giving some basic reminders about membership interviews and identifying things that we are not looking for as evidence of conversion, Burnette provides four questions to help us evaluate whether a prospective member has been converted. Editor’s Note: This article is taken from Church Matters, the 9Marks journal for pastors, in the issue titled Conversion . “I wasn’t living right. I was getting drunk, partying, just doing whatever I wanted. And then it was like God just stopped me in my tracks. I knew something had to change. That’s when I started coming to church, and one Sunday, I felt like the preacher was talking directly to me. Right then I knew I needed to become a Christian, and I got baptized a few weeks later. That was about a year ago, and ever since then I’ve pretty much been coming to church and trying to do what’s right.” That’s how Ben responded when you asked him how he became a Christian. Ben recently moved to your city, and he just completed your church’s four-week New Members Class. Now, as the final step in the process—often called a “membership interview”—you as a pastor must decide whether you will recommend Ben for membership at the next members’ meeting. For the purposes of this article, I’m concerned primarily with the question of whether Ben is converted. I’m assuming he meets your church’s other membership requirements. No doubt you’ve heard similar testimonies, even if the details differ. There’s been some kind of change in the person’s life, and they seem sincere, but it’s not yet clear that this change was rooted in the gospel. So you’ll need to do some more probing. Putting Our Doctrine of Conversion to Work Testimonies like Ben’s remind us why having a biblical doctrine of conversion is so crucial when it comes to the church’s responsibility to affirm new members as believers. After all, it’s difficult to discern whether someone has been converted if you’re hazy on what conversion is . For an explanation of the doctrine of conversion, see Michael Lawrence, Conversion (Crossway, 2017); see also the article by Gregg Allison titled “You Can’t Make I t Happen: The Spirit and the Doctrine of Conversion” in this issue of Church Matters . Testimonies like Ben’s also remind us that we must be able to apply our doctrine of conversion to real-life people in real-life situations. Some prospective members will be new Christians, while others will be less mature in their faith; some will have been converted for years but still have significant blind spots; still others will think they’re Christians when they haven’t truly been converted. And those aren’t the only complicating factors. Some will have a hard time articulating the very truths they profess; others will fail to mention basic aspects of the gospel in their interview; more than a few will be unsure as to how and when they recognized their need for a Savior. All these factors (and more) mean that wisdom and discernment are needed when we are interviewing prospective members. Reminders for Our Approach Before thinking through some practical ways to probe further with testimonies like Ben’s, a few basic reminders may be helpful. Your Knowledge Is Limited Unlike Jesus, we can’t look into a person’s heart, which means our decisions about someone’s spiritual state are never infallible. The very fact that Jesus gave instructions about excommunication indicates that he knew the church would sometimes welcome in those who weren’t truly converted (see Matt. 18:15–18). Even the apostle Paul was wrong about his one-time co-worker Demas. Prior to Demas’s departure, Paul mentions him twice when he refers to his fellow workers in the gospel ministry (Col. 4:14; Ph lm. 24). Ou

articles.title: Unclear Evangelism Leads to Unclear (and False) Conversions
articles.summary: When we appeal to people’s carnal desires, we should not be surprised when our “converts” are more in love with the world than with our Savior.   The post  Unclear Evangelism Leads to Unclear (and False) Conversions  appeared first on  9Marks .
articles.summary_zh: 当我们呼吁人们的肉体渴望时，当我们的「皈依者」更爱世界而不是我们的救主时，我们不应该感到惊讶。“不明确的传福音导致不明确（和虚假）的转换”一文首先出现在9Marks上。
articles.title_zh: 不明确的传福音会导致不明确（和虚假）的皈依
articles.content: Abstract: John Lee explains how bad evangelistic methods and approaches can lead to false conversions. When we are unclear about the urgency of conversion, the cost of conversion, or the accountability that should accompany conversion, we risk leaving people deceived about their eternal state. Ultimately, our job is simply to proclaim the gospel clearly, trust God to open people’s hearts to the truth, and provide ongoing discipleship to those who respond in repentance and faith. Editor’s Note: This article is taken from Church Matters, the 9Marks journal for pastors, in the issue titled Conversion . Maybe you’re like me and you grew up in a church that did altar calls. My church’s zeal for evangelism was real, and I can still tell you the names of individuals who came to know the Lord through those gospel presentations. But like me, you may also have walked down the aisle to accept Jesus as your Lord and Savior at least five times. The thing is, I believe I was sincere every time I walked the aisle. So why do it over and over again? There was clearly a misunderstanding, despite my church’s good intentions—and my own. The methodology of our ministry affects the fruit of our ministry. Or as Mark Dever has put it, “What you win them with is what you win them to .” Unclear invitations often lead to confused converts. Below I want to consider three different ways this lack of clarity in our evangelism manifests itself and how this can lead to conversions that, in time, prove themselves false. Unclear Urgency I was a disobedient kid. When my mother was particularly exasperated, she’d count down from ten. I had a choice: either obey or dig my heels in and rebel. But as I grew older, I became immune to her shot clock and more accustomed to her threats. My mom’s words fell on deaf ears. Bad evangelism capitalizes on this kind of “countdown” strategy. It puts eternity in the balance based on a singular moment and a one-time decision to follow God—or abandon him forever. And while unbelievers may initially respond positively, their “faith” often doesn’t last. As a result, they may become immune to the gospel because they assume they’ve already tried it. “But,” you might say, “isn’t conversion an urgent matter? Do we not care about people’s eternal destiny?” Absolutely! But we want to place appropriate pressure on their conscience, not just on their choice. Unbelievers need to make a thoughtful decision rather than simply meeting our demands in a singular moment in time. Panic urges them to turn off their critical thinking for the sake of survival. The focus is on an immediate decision rather than the weight of God’s eternal judgment. Unclear Cost At the same time, panicked evangelism is sometimes replaced with what we might call chill evangelism. Chill evangelism attempts to downplay urgency in order to make the decision to follow Jesus more palatable. To take one example, some recent invitations have defined following Jesus as “doing as he did.” The call is to adopt his behavior, particularly his compassion toward the brokenhearted. But following Jesus is about more than adopting a certain kind of spirituality and lifestyle; it’s also about salvation from the judgment of a holy God. Nor is it something you can dabble in; it requires real sacrifice. Jesus says in Matthew 10:38, “Whoever doesn’t take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.” As Bonhoeffer famously said, “When Christ calls a man, he bids him come and die.” Dietrich Bonhoeffer, The Cost of Discipleship (Simon Schuster, 1959), 89. Conversion costs something. Saying yes to Jesus means saying no to sin, to our own passions, and to our former life. The question is: Does our evangelism draw attention to what people must give up? Conversion doesn’t propel us further toward our goals. Rather, it fundamentally reframes our goals in light of God’s kingdom. When we appeal to people’s carnal desires, we should not be surprised when our “converts” are more in love with the world

articles.title: What Conversion Looks Like in Messy People (Like Me)
articles.summary: All sinners, regardless of past trauma, messiness of life, socioeconomic background, or educational attainment must be converted the same way—through repentance and faith in Christ alone.    The post  What Conversion Looks Like in Messy People (Like Me)  appeared first on  9Marks .
articles.summary_zh: 所有罪人，无论过去的创伤、生活的混乱、社会经济背景或教育程度如何，都必须通过悔改和对基督的信心以同样的方式皈依。帖子What Conversion Looks Like in Messy People (Like Me)首次出现在9Marks上。
articles.title_zh: 乱七八糟的人（像我一样）的转化是什么样子
articles.content: Abstract: Mez McConnell points out that the fruit of conversion looks different in everyone’s life, particularly for those who come out of difficult, or “messy,” backgrounds. McConnell illustrates this point by giving two contrasting conversion stories. Then, based on his own background and his ministry among others with difficult backgrounds, he offers five reminders to help pastors minister to such individuals and discern whether they have, in fact, been converted. Editor’s Note: This article is taken from Church Matters, the 9Marks journal for pastors, in the issue titled Conversion . If you’ve been a pastor for a while, it’s likely that you’ve seen some people convert from difficult backgrounds. The Lord saved me from a very difficult past and has given me a ministry to many who come from a similar place. In this piece, I am going to share two conversion stories: one “clean” story and one messy. In God’s kindness to me, I have seen people like John and Jane (who you’re soon to meet) come to saving faith through the witness of my local church. In considering the similarities and differences in John and Jane’s conversions, I pray you grow in boldness, discernment, and patience as you faithfully proclaim the gospel and help people live it out in their own lives. John, a college student who has been attending your Sunday services for some time, asks to speak with you. You meet up and he tells you about his growing conviction over his sin and of his need to repent and place his faith in Christ (those aren’t the terms he uses, but that’s what he means). You feel sure that he is being genuine and so you pray with him and urge him to trust in Christ. Soon after, John tells you that he is now a Christian and so you put him in touch with a mature believer in the church to begin the discipleship process. As the weeks and months progress, you begin to observe a real spiritual hunger in John as he devours the Bible, attends a small group, and comes regularly to a class on Christian doctrine. John begins to pray earnestly in the public meetings, and he volunteers to serve the church body in a number of different ways. So far, so good. John appears to be “soundly converted.” Conversion Doesn’t Always Look the Same Now, let’s change the story to Jane, a single mom of three with an addiction to cannabis and prescription painkillers. What does conversion look like for her? Should we think about “lowering the bar” for people like Jane from so-called “messy” backgrounds? In other words, should we expect less spiritual fruit from Jane than we do from John? And should we expect the spiritual maturation process to be slower, too? Back to Jane and her cannabis and pill addiction. She is in your office talking about feeling convicted of sin and of her desire to put her faith in Jesus for salvation (again, those aren’t the terms she uses, but that’s what she means). As with John, you feel that she is being genuine, and when she tells you a short time later that she’s now trusting in Jesus, you put her in touch with a mature lady in the church to disciple her. However, unlike John, Jane is irregular when it comes to attending Sunday services. Often she turns up late, if she bothers turning up at all. When she does appear, the children are normally loud and fidgety and cause all manner of distractions to those around them. A few members have commented that there is often a strong smell coming off her when she sits near them (later identified as cannabis). When asked about how she is doing spiritually, she becomes very animated about her faith and is proud of the fact that she has drastically cut down her cannabis consumption. The lady who has been discipling Jane reports that she is sporadic in her attendance at Bible study and that she has only been to one small group meeting since professing faith in Christ. You start to have doubts about the genuineness of Jane’s conversion. Things come to a head one evening when a church member calls to inform yo
articles.content_zh: 摘要:Mez McConnell指出,皈依的果实在每个人的生活中都不同,对那些从困难或 " 迷思 " 背景中出来的人来说尤其如此。 McConnell通过给出两个对比的转换故事来说明这一点. 然后,他根据自己的背景以及他的部会和其他有困难背景的人,提出5个提醒,帮助牧师部长向这些人提供帮助,并查明他们是否实际上已经皈依。 编辑说明:这篇文章取自9Marks牧师杂志《教会事务》, 如果你做了一段时间的牧师, 你可能已经看到一些人从困难的背景皈依。 上帝把我从一个非常艰难的过去中拯救出来,并且给了我一个部属给来自类似地方的许多人. 在这部作品中,我将分享两个转换故事:一个是“干净的”故事,一个是混乱的。 我看见约翰和珍(你们很快会见到他们)这样的人, 在考虑约翰和简的皈依过程中的相似之处和差异时,我祈祷你在忠实地宣示福音并帮助人们在自己的生活中生活的同时,以大胆、分辨和耐心地成长。 约翰,一个大学生 他一直在参加你的星期天服务 一段时间,要求与你说话。 他告诉大家,他越来越相信自己的罪过,需要忏悔和信仰基督(这些不是他所用的条件,而是他的意思)。 你确信他是真的 所以你和他一起祈祷 并且敦促他相信基督 不久,约翰告诉你,他现在是基督徒,所以你让他与教会中成熟的信徒联系,开始门徒礼仪过程. 随着数周和数月的进步,你开始在约翰吞噬"圣经"时,观察到一个真正的精神饥饿,参加了一个小团体,并定期来到一个有关基督教教义的班级. 约翰开始在公开会议上真诚祈祷,他自愿以多种不同的方式为教会机构服务. 目前还不错 约翰看来是“貌似被转化了 ” 。 我们改编成Jane的故事, 她的皈依是什么样子? 我们是否应该考虑让Jane这种来自所谓“迷信”背景的人“降低律师资格”? 换句话说,我们是否应该期望简的精神果实比约翰少? 我们是否应期望精神成熟的过程也放慢? 回到简和她大麻和药瘾。 她正在你办公室里谈论被判定有罪的感觉, 以及她希望相信耶稣以救赎的愿望(这又不是她使用的术语, 与约翰一样,你觉得她很真实,当她稍后告诉你她现在信任耶稣时,你让她在教堂里与一位成熟的女士联系,让她成为门徒。 然而,与约翰不同的是,简在参加星期天礼拜时是不规则的. 她经常迟到,如果她烦恼的话。 当她出现时,孩子们通常声音大而虚无,给周围的人带来各种分心。 少数成员评论说,当她坐在他们(后来被确定为大麻)附近时,经常有强烈的气味从她身上冒出. 当被问到她的精神状况时,她变得非常动画化她的信仰,并对她大幅度削减了大麻消费感到骄傲. 这位纪律严明的女士报告说,她偶尔参加《圣经》的学习,自从她表示相信基督以来,她只参加了一次小组会议。 你开始对简的皈依的真实性产生怀疑。 某天晚上,当一个教会成员打电话通知你时,事情就变得头疼了

articles.title: The Reason for Church: A Review
articles.summary: Rescue us from ourselves? No. Jesus died to rescue us from God’s wrath.    The post  The Reason for Church: A Review  appeared first on  9Marks .
articles.summary_zh: 把我们从自己手中解救出来？不，耶稣死是为了把我们从神的愤怒中拯救出来。帖子The Reason for Church: A Review首先出现在9Marks上。
articles.title_zh: 建立教会的原因：回顾
articles.content: Abstract: Paul Alexander reviews Brad Edwards’s book The Reason for Church , highlighting strengths of the book’s cultural diagnosis while also identifying weaknesses in its prescription for how our current problems should be addressed by the church and the gospel. Edwards emphasizes how sin has affected the way we relate to one another, but he does not adequately address the way our sin affects our relationship with God. Readers will benefit from many of Edwards’s insights, but those who believe that the church’s primary mission is to make disciples through the proclamation of the gospel will find substantive areas of disagreement with his view of the church and its mission. Brad Edwards, The Reason for Church: Why the Body of Christ Still Matters in an Age of Anxiety, Division, and Radical Individualism . Zondervan, 2025. 240 pp. When many of us first read David Wells’s No Place for Truth back in the day, we felt like we did when we saw our first Trans Am. You know who you are—don’t deny it. I know, Christian cultural analysis is more than just “cool” or “awesome.” It’s public theology for evangelism. But shouldn’t it be at least a little thrilling to apply Christian logic to public trends? The world never tires of rephrasing the Serpent’s question, “Did God really say . . .?” Our age now rallies around a therapeutic spirituality, justified by victimhood as a new virtue, expressed through social media, aflame with anti-institutionalism. That leaves the local church looking so . . . 1900s, which implies we need not just a reason for God but a reason for church. The title of Brad Edwards’s book, The Reason for Church , tips us off that Edwards hews more to the apologetics of Tim Keller than to the systematics of David Wells. Edwards is an intellectually sophisticated critic of the meta-modern malaise. Thankfully, he loves Christ and the church more than anything in this world. He pastors The Table, a PCA congregation in Colorado that subscribes to the Westminster Confession of Faith. This book earned Christianity Today’s 2025 Book of the Year for its well-informed cultural analysis, penetrating insights, shrewd applications, and flecks of gospel gold. After reading it, I was not surprised to learn The Reason for Church also earned Edwards The Gospel Coalition First-Time Author Award. Edwards turns phrases like pancakes, but he’s not a show-off. He’s heartfelt, and he’s got personal stories from ministry in his own local church that verify and illustrate his analysis and applications. He writes like he’s done this before. Approach Edwards articulates his social critique of late modernity as Burkean conservatism, focused through the political lens of Yuval Levin and Jonah Goldberg, filtered through the sociological insight of Charles Murray, and lit by the psychological findings of Jonathan Haidt. The “little platoons” of local mediating institutions that put us shoulder to shoulder with people across the political aisle are disappearing (79, 93; think Putnam’s Bowling Alone ). We are fracturing the republic into politically homogeneous ghettos by ZIP code. With no buffer between the individual and the political, everything becomes political, impersonal, ultimate . . . and contentious. Diagnosis Today, individualism hijacks individuality such that self becomes sacrosanct. Boomers built churches on Peter Drucker’s pragmatism, which ended up offering Sunday consumers “a Coldplay concert with a TED talk” (14, 16). The church’s customer-is-king technique only manipulates our Main Character Syndrome, making church a provider of goods and services, and excusing us for treating each other as non-player participants in a reality where self is still the star of the show (47–48). Therapy teaches us to prize intuitional over institutional spiritualities (28–35, channeling Philip Rieff and Carl Trueman), so people retreat from churches that call them to repent, choosing instead safe spaces that affirm them in sin. Social media disintegrates
articles.content_zh: 摘要:保罗·亚历山大评论了布拉德·爱德华兹所著"教会的理由"一书,强调了该书文化诊断的优点,同时也指出了该书如何由教会和福音书解决我们当前问题处方的弱点. Edwards强调罪恶如何影响我们彼此的关系,但他没有充分处理我们的罪恶如何影响我们与上帝的关系。 读者将会从爱德华兹的许多见解中获益,但那些认为教会的首要使命是通过宣示福音来培养门徒的人会发现他对于教会及其使命的看法存在实质性的分歧. 布拉德·爱德华兹 《教会的理由:为什么基督的身体在焦虑、分裂和激进个人主义的时代仍然重要》,Zondervan,2025年。 当我们许多人第一次读到大卫·威尔斯的《真理无所归宿》时, 你知道自己是谁, 我知道,基督教文化分析不仅仅是“酷”或“优美”的。 这是福音派的公共神学。 将基督教逻辑运用到公众潮流中, 世界从未厌倦重写蛇人的问题,“上帝真的说过吗?” 我们这个时代现在围绕着一种治疗性精神, 以受害者为理由, 这让当地教会看起来如此 1900年代,这意味着我们不仅需要上帝的理由,还需要教会的理由. Brad Edwards的书标题是《教会的理由》, 爱德华兹是一位在知识上精密的批评者,对"元-现代"的弊病进行了批判. 谢天谢地,他更爱基督和教会,比世界上任何事物都要多. 他在科罗拉多州的一个常设仲裁法院会众中担任牧师,赞同威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔书。 这本书赢得了基督教今日2025年的"年度之书",因为它有丰富的文化分析、深入的见解、精通的应用以及福音黄金的花纹。 在读完之后,我并不惊讶地得知"教会的理由"也获得了爱德华兹福音联盟的"第一次作者奖". Edwards的口味就像煎饼, 他的内心深处, 他写得像以前一样。 接近爱德华兹阐述他对后期现代主义的社会批评为伯克南保守主义,通过尤瓦尔·莱文和约拿·高德伯格的政治透镜来聚焦,通过查尔斯·默里的社会学见解来过滤,并被乔纳森·海德的心理发现所点燃. 当地调解机构的“小排”让我们与政治道上的人并肩并肩(79,93;认为普特南的保龄球是孤独的 ) 。 根据ZIP代码,我们把共和国分裂成政治上单一的犹太区。 在个人和政治之间没有缓冲,一切都变成政治的,非人性的,终极的.和有争议. 今天的诊断,个性主义劫持了个性,以至于自我变得神圣. Boomers根据彼得·德鲁克的实用主义建造了教堂,最终提供星期天的消费者们“与TED谈话的冷戏音乐会”(14,16)。 教会的顾客-王牌技术只操控了我们的主要性格综合症,使教会成为商品和服务的提供者,并责怪我们在现实中将对方视为非玩家参与者,而现实中自我仍然是节目的主角(47–48). 治疗教导我们把直觉的奖赏给制度性精神(28–35,引导菲利普·里夫和卡尔·特鲁曼),因此人们从号召他们悔改的教堂中退缩,选择了安全的地方来证实他们的罪恶。 社交媒体解体
